However, the miscreants managed to escape from the location, taking advantage of low illumination and wild vegetation. They left behind approximately 50-60 kg of stolen iron scrap. Fortunately, our security team successfully recovered the material from the scene and Police compliant logged against the miscreants.

INCIDENTTITLE: ASSET/PROPERTY at BALCO site at 05 Sep 2023, 2:00 PM
INCIDENTDETAILS: On September 5th, 2023, we were informed of theft incidents involving the pilferage of PPEs from the Foundry's Store, located within the foundry area. The report was provided by the Store In charge, Mr. Gaya Prasad. Upon receiving this information, our security team-initiated a thorough investigation by analyzing the CCTV footage. The review revealed that between 1300 to 1400 hours, during Mr. Gaya Prasad's lunch break, two individuals consistently accessed the store. They would open the store, remove PPEs, and then securely lock it afterward. Subsequent analysis identified the culprits as Mr. Kishor (UID: 20985), an apprentice working under Mr. Gaya Prasad, and Mr. Amrendra Singh (UID: 1546278 M/s Surendra Engineering). Mr. Kishor's familiarity with the store's key placement allowed him to access it during Mr. Gaya Prasad's absence. He would then contact Mr. Amrendra Singh, who would collect the stolen PPEs. After retrieving the PPEs, Mr. Amrendra Singh would proceed directly to the melting area, while Mr. Kishor returned to the In-charge office to reposition the keys at their designated location. This pattern of theft began on July 23rd and continued July 25th, 27th, 28th, and 31st. The thefts also extended into August, occurring on the 7th, 8th, 9th, and 12th of the month. Additionally, it has come to our attention that the stolen PPEs were subsequently sold by the perpetrators to another worker, Mr. Surendra Kumar Kaushik (UID: 1545518 M/s Parekh Engineering). Mr. Kaushik established a fixed price for various PPE items, offering 200 rupees each for Face Shields and Gloves and 500 rupees for each Balaclava.

INCIDENTTITLE: ASSET/PROPERTY at RAM Agucha site at 30 Nov 2023, 7:00 PM
INCIDENTDETAILS:
An incident involving the theft of diesel from a crane, Reg. No.RJ14EA5119, owned by M/S Monomark. On 30/11/2023 at about the 1900hrs , we received reliable intelligence regarding the occurrence of diesel theft from a specific crane located near the patrol pump at Rupaheli Circle Corner. In response, our Quick Response Team (QRT) promptly mobilized, accompanied by Mr. Mittusingh, the Administrative Officer of the security agency M/S G4S .
Upon reaching the reported location, our team noticed the crane heading towards the mine and immediately pursued it. They successfully tracked the crane to the mine circle, where they apprehended the driver. Subsequently, an investigation led by Deputy CSO Ajay Sharma was initiated.
The investigation revealed that the driver, identified as Harman Singh From Gurdaspur (Punjab) with license number PB5820200000161, accepted responsibility for pilfering approximately 60 liters of diesel. He confessed to selling the stolen diesel to a local shop owner who specializes in vehicle repairs. Harman Singh, a resident of Gurdaspur, Punjab, has been entering the site using a service engineer gate pass for the past 15 days. It is worth noting that the crane is operated by M/S Shree Ganesh Crane Services, a subcontractor of M/S Monomark.
The incident took place on 30/11/2023 when the crane was dispatched to the ZLD plant located outside the mine at approximately 1600 hrs on proper NRGP. However, the driver deviated from the assigned task and diverted to Rupaheli Circle at around 1900 hrs with the intention of theft. As a result, the driver has been handed over to the Gulabpura Police Station for further investigation and legal proceedings.

INCIDENTTITLE: Workers strike due to salary delay at SILVASSA site at 05 Mar 2024, 6:00 AM
INCIDENTDETAILS:
On 05th March 2023, at about 0600hrs around 35 monomark employees of A shift gathered near main gate and refused to go on work, due to non-payment of salary wages. Immediately B Madhan Kumar along with QRT and security team deployed at main gate. Security officer passed information to the Head Security, and Security SIC informed to the CCPC SIC, Refinery SIC and CCR SIC. OHC informed by Control room operator. Head security informed to the BU COO, IR and HR head. At 0630hrs, around 10 C-shift employees of Monomark also joined the gathering at main gate. At 0709hrs Monomark Site Head Mr Prashant Naik reported and convinced workers to go to work stating that their salary will happen EOD. Further, at 0712hrs Monomark employees reported to duty peacefully. At 0915hrs, around 15 G-shift Monomark employees gathered outside main gate, Security SIC informed to the Head Security, Head HR and Head IR. At 0930hrs Monomark HR Vaishali Pandya, and Prashant Naik convinced them and further they reported to their duty.

On 06th March 2023, 0610hrs 50-60 Monomark Employees gathered near main gate since their wages did not credit as promised by management. Security team deployed at the gate immediately. At 0620hrs necessary communication done to the Head HR, Head PR, COO and Monomark Management. At 0645hrs Peregrine area manager also reached at the site. At 0654hrs Mr Prashant Naik reached and tried to convince workers, but workers refused to go back on work. At 0808hrs Head PR Mr Joshi and Head HR Mr Saket reached on the site and stated that wages would be credited by 7th March 2023. Further, Monomark personal resumed duty peacefully at 0830hrs.

INCIDENTTITLE: Any Other at IRON ORE ORISSA site at 14 Dec 2023, 12:00 AM
INCIDENTDETAILS:
Theft Incident at IOO: Pilferage of 5/18mm CLO at Nadidihi Iron & Mn Ore mine, IOO dated 14.12.2023.

Incident Reporting: 
The PC operator known as Amulya Munda informed the Logistics shift Incharge, Mr.Lal Babu Rai  between 00. 15 hrs to 00.30 hrs(15.12.2023) that one Truck, No. NL01AE6260 (22-wheeler) came to the weighbridge heavily overloaded carrying CLO 5-18mm. This truck came to the weighbridge no 4 platform but went without doing any weight adjustment. He noticed that the external display of the weighbridge was OFF.  He expected that this truck would come back to the weighbridge for weighment. When this truck did not come back for weighment but went outside the gate, he got suspicious and hence informed the Logistic Supervisor incharge of the Shift Mr. Lal Babu Rai who was present at the Security cum Document printing Cabin where documents are printed.    

Lal Babu Rai promptly took the security QRT team assistance and started chasing.  Meanwhile they contacted the transporter and asked to Hold the truck and informed the Transporter not to make the LR.  The Transporter confirmed that they have informed the driver not to proceed. The team found the truck parked at Bhadrasahi (about 20 km) from the mine. The Driver did not respond to the calls from the Transporters after this incident. 

The team decided to get back the truck to the mine & the Truck was brought back and parked at the mines by arranging other driver(by transporter) at about 3.00 am on 15th Dec. The Truck weighed 18 tons more than the Gross weight on the Documents. 

The truck was dispatched with TP No: L22301186/11.  Gross weight: 56.940, Net weight 40.140.   TP timing: 11:26pm   Name of the Consigner: Red Mountain Minerals (trader), End User: Anindita Steels Limited Senegarh, Jharkand. 

As the truck was found to be carrying ore more than that mentioned in the Transit permit, it was decided by IOO Exco that the case needs to be investigated. 


Investigating team:   Camilo Fernandes with Logistics Team, Uday Verma -Security, Vivek Sambrekar (Operations), Jaidev Mandal – IT (for video footage from Weighbridge Camera).

Investigation Proceedings:  
1)	All 4 weighbridges at the mine are manned by NSIPL staff for Transit pass generation. There is no IOO persons at the weighbridges all the time and only the IOO supervisor on duty makes rounds on need basis or casual rounds.  The Third-party persons deployed from our end(AD-ashtra) are engaged for document printing(Transit Pass, invoice, e-way bill) at Exit point/Security gate.  
2)	The weighbridge Operator (Dharmendra Kanungo, employee of NSIPL) on duty at the time of Incidence went absconding as soon as the case came in to light and before the truck was bought back.   
3)	The PC 71 operator at W/B known as Amulya Munda (deployed by NSIPL) was called to the mines in the morning(15.12.23) and he narrated the same incident as described above.  He further said that one more Truck 4073 approached him to give him more tonnage or said something which he could not understand but he adjusted the load as per process and the truck went of the weighbridge.  He said he would sign this statement once ready and wanted to go back immediately for some personal exigencies. 
4)	The Security gate CCTV Camera footage was checked and it was seen that this truck-6260 entered the Mine at around 20.00 hrs (Security ingate physical record is 19.53 hrs of 14th Dec). 
5)	There is no Security CCTV footage after Entry. The next footage of this truck on Security CCTV shows the Exit time around 23.32 hrs 
6)	In line with the narration of incidence by PC operator at Weigh bridge, the loading Operator Dushmanto Mahanto at stack and the Site Supervisor Mr.Dulal Kumar Pani were asked about the incident. As per both of them there was nothing unusual about the truck that loaded 5-18 CLO but Wheel loader operator Mahanto faintly remembers that one truck was asking for extra load and he just loaded half a bucket and asked the driver to go as he was sure that the truck was loaded enough (by his experience). He refused to accept that he can overload any truck to the extent of 18 tons.  
7)	The site Supervisor said that he does not keep a record of trucks loaded at a site but just keeps a count of trucks and that 12 trucks were loaded from 2 pm till 12 pm.
8)	Other concerned supervisors in the rank at NSIPL also said that there was no abnormal or unusual matter on that day regarding truck loading at CLO stack as only 11 to 12 trucks were loaded. The Mine Incharge of NSIPL Mr.Durga Prasad reiterate internal opinion that seeing the truck load which is evenly spread, the same is difficult to achieve with Wheel loader and it looks to be the work of excavator. He confirms that there was no excavator deployed for loading the truck in the second shift for loading 5-18 CLO. Only one truck was loaded with excavator that too in shift 3. 
9)	Mr. Jaidev Mandal was then asked to retrieve the CCTV camera footage from the weighbridge 4. It may be noted that these WB camera footages get recorded locally at weigh bridge and not centrally.
10)	Observation from WB CCTV Camera: 
a)	WB CCTV camera timing has a lag of 12 to 13 minutes from the i3MS time.
b)	The Particular truck 6260 came to the WB platform at around 22.15.  The indicator display goes off.  The WB operator seems to be communicating with the PC operator and the PC operator immediately starts to load the truck abnormally and adds about 25 to 30 buckets to load the truck fully till the container top evenly spread. The trucks moves out of the weighbridge at around 22.40 hrs (WB camera time). However as per i3MS records there is no transaction of this truck during this time interval (after adjustment of time difference). So it is inferred that the transaction was not made at that point of time. 
c)	Two more trucks weighed including truck no. 4073. It is seen that some discussion taking place with the diver of MH12UM-4073, the Weighbridge Operator and the PC Operator. 
d)	It is later seen that around 23.11 hrs one truck RJ47GA4438 (having the 55 GVW capacity vs  NL01AE6260 ie 57 tons ) destined to Bokaro enters the weighbridge Platform, the PC operator starts to adjust the weight and the truck leaves the WB platform at 23.24 hrs .   (during this time duration considering the time lag, it is seen that two transactions (ie TP challan of two trucks, one of NL01AE6260 and other of RJ47GA4438) are created. Hence it is inferred that the Weighbrdge Operator has made two transactions keeping RJ47GA4438 on W/B. First transaction is made of NL01AE6260 and then within a minute of RJ47GA4438. 
e)	On 19th Dec, the PC operator has given a statement that is recorded in camera - He says that after the display went off, the Weighbridge operator asked him to load till he instructs to stop.  He has done accordingly but as he sensed something wrong, he reported the incident to our people at security gate. He delayed to inform as there were continuous trucks reporting at the weighbridge for top-up.
f)	MDO ie NSIPL site incharge Mr.Prashant Sinha has seen the video footage on 18th Dec 23 and agreed the involvement of his staff i.e the WB operator and the PC operator. Prior to this, on 16th evening the incident was communicated to MDO owner Mr. Vinay Passary for looking into the matter.
g)	On 19th Dec 23, the Trader Red Mountain Minerals/Transporter engaged by Trader M/s Hindustan Transport and our MDO are asked to give a written statement on this incident. Response from the trader received at around18hrs on 19.12.2023.

Findings and Root Cause  

1)	Three people seem to be involved in this pilferage case. The WB-4 Operator Dharmendra Kanugo, The Truck driver, and the PC operator.
2)	The involvement of any other person not established in the investigation till now. MDO incharge, Mr. Sinha mentioned that they will investigate the matter further by taking help of Police without lodging FIR.
3)	There are loopholes in the system as the truck ID is fed manually

INCIDENTTITLE: Unauthorized entry/ Intrusion/Trespassing at TUTICORIN site at 2024-07-26 00:30
INCIDENTDETAILS:
On the intervening night of 25/26th July 2024 at 0030hrs a message was received from security guard of OS parking duty post that a person was roaming with a Billhook (Long sword) outside parking to Tamria#1 town ship gate. Message flashed to shift I/c SO Ramamurthy and Security HoD G Mallesham. In turn as per HoD's instructions the matter was informed to out Post Police of the area. Duty SO has accompanied the police to the spot and apprehended the person. Further on investigation by the police it is learnt that the person belongs to TV Puram and his name is Mr. Ramar and motive for venturing in the location was not revealed. Thereafter, police taken him to their custody along with the sword. As per the latest information on the matter the person is mentally disturbed and after counselling police let him off without registering any FIR/entry.
Note:-  Photos uploaded but not reflecting in the ISIMS portal report

Action taken: 
1.	The Security Team swiftly acted upon the incident and alerted the police and assisted them in apprehending the person.

Measures implemented to prevent such occurrences

1.	Security patrolling has been increased in and around Tamira#1 and OS parking area.  
2.	Night guards at lone post are briefed and ensured personal safety measures.
3.	Communication equipment such as mobile phones, whistles and torch lights were ensured at all lone guard duty posts.

INCIDENTTITLE: Perimeter wall collapse due to excessive rainfall at SILVASSA site on 19 Jun 2025, 12:40 PM
INCIDENTDETAILS: On 19th June 2025 at approx. 1240hrs, Traffic Marshall Anshu Singh reported via radio that the perimeter wall between BW no 69 and 70 had collapsed. Upon receiving the message, Security SIC Sweta Kumari and Head Security Heramb Joshi promptly arrived at the incident site. It was determined that the wall had been obscured by bushes for an extended period, and its base had been further weakened due to excessive rainfall in Silvassa. Head Security passed information to Head Civil Department AV Durgaprasad, Head External Affairs Kiran Joshi, and IBU Director Sathiya Narayanmoorthy. To address the situation promptly, it was decided to install GI sheets and Civil Engineer Sankalp Deshmukh was assigned the responsibility.

At around 2203 hrs, QRT member SG Sanjay Patley observed suspicious behaviour from a worker exiting through the Alumina 2W Out Gate, who escaped when approached. Upon noticing the security presence, the miscreants abandoned the aluminium scrap they were attempting to steal and fled the scene. CCTV footage identified the suspect as Mr. Mukesh Kumar (ID: 1604528), an employee of M/s Lizmontagens India. The team recovered 53 kgs of aluminium scrap, which has been stored securely. The matter has been escalated to the HR department, and the gate pass of the identified individual has been blocked pending further investigation.

INCIDENTTITLE: Misdemeanour by Ex-SS at Piparia
INCIDENTDETAILS:
On 26th May 2023, at around 07.40pm SCR operator Abhishek Singh informed SIC Parvathi that logistics person in Piparia Anand had called him for vehicle entry as he could not find the security supervisor. On inquiring it was found that ex-SS Satyaprakash had left his post vacant and left the plant premises, without informing Piparia plant head and/or SIC in Chinchpada.

The Peregrine area officer Ajit and site-incharge of Peregrine Jitendra were informed, and immediately they reached the site and vehicle movement was ensured with due check. At around 08.40pm Supevisor Satyaprakash returned back to premises. It was noticed that the supervisor had consumed alcohol. Peregrine team enquired about the same and asked him to leave the location. 

SIC from Chinchpada reached Piparia at 08.55pm to inquire about the situation and take control of the logistics movement. It was found that Satyaprakash had asked housekeeping person Dilip Kherwa and signed his outgate pass to go outside, on his motorbike. Satyaprakash had ‘wanted to go to Bhilad to find a relative who had run away from home’- as per his statement. Following this, security guard Jayshree took up the post at main gate, but due to inability to perform system work, they were unable to make vehicle entries, because of which logistics SIC Anand had to call Abhishek Singh in Chinchpada.

Night shift SIC Vinush Kadali reported at plant at 09.15pm and took over security operations and all clear was given at 09.20pm.

INCIDENTTITLE: Scuffle between 3 persons in ACP washroom at silvassa site at 13 Sep 2023, 11:11 AM
INCIDENTDETAILS: On 11/09/2023 at 11:15 am Mr. Jay Prakash from fabrication mechanical went to the ACP rest room to refresh himself, where PMB helper Mr. Ajit Wagh was washing his face in the wash basin. During that time water splashed on Jay Prakash who was standing near the wash basin. A heated argument ensued between the two and Ajit Wagh groped Jayprakash’s neck tightly, with his hand. At that moment, Mr.Jaglal, fabrication mechanical, co-worker of Jayprakash, walked into the washroom and found them scuffling. Jaglal interfered into the fight, and an argument started between the Ajit Wagh and Jaglal. Then Ajit Wagh caught hold of Jaglal’s neck tightly. Jaglal, feeling suffocated, bit Ajit on his right arm very hard. Following the fight, Ajit Wagh told Jaglal and Jayprakash that this should be reported to the supervisor, but both Jaglal and Jayprakash refused to do so. Ajit Wagh complained to the Monomark supervisor about the events, and the communication reached the Security Shift Officer via the fabrication security guard. The investigation was concluded, with all three persons accepting their misdoings.

INCIDENTTITLE: Incidents against personnel at silvassa site at 16 Sep 2023, 7:00 PM
INCIDENTDETAILS: At 19.05 hours the security team was notified regarding a scuffle that ensued between two Monomark employees working in the Refinery, Mr. Raju Devidas Jadhao and Mr. Ajay Prasad. Both were involved in a verbal duel, followed by physically holding each other’s necks, which was resolved by a VL employee. After investigation at gate, it was found that Raju had asked Ajay to wear apron while shifting plates, due to which Ajay used curse words at him, which led to a verbal fight, and eventually held each other’s neck. We were also notified that Mr. Raju was consuming tobacco during the incident, which was confirmed during investigation, when we found the packet of tobacco in his possession. Statements from both the people were taken, and both have admitted to their mistakes.

At 19:46hrs, it was observed that Mr. Ramkawal Yadav, forklift operator, parked the fork lift near lug cutting area at CCPC and sneaked into the lug cutting area after turning off his forklift. He placed a piece of cloth on a copper lug piece and picked the piece up. Further, he hidden the lug piece at the fork of his forklift, he took the forklift and parked it near the CCPC washroom area. He stopped his forklift, took the hidden material out from the fork, hid the piece inside his safety helmet, and he was about to sneak into the washroom. Right in front of the washroom, at 19:52hrs, he was caught by Mr. Nandkishore Patel and SG Shafik Khan, and the material was recovered from his possession. He was interrogated in the Security cabin head Security Ananda and SIC Nandkishore, to which he confessed and provided his statement to the SIC where he accepted his mistake.

Action taken: Increased more time to patrolling in that area.

INCIDENTTITLE: Material at BALCO site at 13 Jun 2023, 7:45 PM
INCIDENTDETAILS: During a routine inspection of vehicles at the Alumina Four Wheeler Gate on June 13th, 2023, Security Guard Mr. Rajeev Ranjan reported an incident. At approximately 19:45 hours, he discovered Fiber optic patch cords in a project vehicle with the registration number CG12 AQ 8379. The vehicle was being driven by Mr. Satyendra Sahu, who is an employee of ABB Power Products and Systems and works under Hitachi Energy India Limited. Upon receiving the aforementioned incident report, a subsequent investigation was conducted, uncovering that the fiber optic patch cords were being utilized for panel relay communication work. On June 13th, 2023, these patch cords were initially stored in Package One Container near the GIS area. As the work progressed, it was planned to relocate the fiber patch cords from Package One Container to Package Two Container near the Petrol Pump, using the vehicle with the registration number CG12 AQ 8379. Both of these containers, Package One and Package Two, belonged to Hitachi Energy. Consequently, the responsibility for loading the fiber optic patch cords into the vehicle with the number CG12 AQ 8379 was assigned to a worker named Mr. Jahed Alam. Mr. Jahed Alam successfully loaded the fiber optic patch cord material onto the vehicle CG12 AQ 8379. However, upon reaching the vehicle's destination, Mr. Jahed Alam failed to unload the fiber optic patch cord material from the vehicle. As a result, the fiber optic patch cord material remained inside the vehicle CG12 AQ 8379 until its arrival at the Alumina Gate. Furthermore, during the departure, the driver, Mr. Satyendra Sahu, also neglected to inspect the vehicle, which led to his apprehension by the Alumina Gate Security. The information regarding the incident was confirmed with the relevant department. Statements were obtained from all individuals involved, and a communication regarding ownership of fibre optic patch cord Material was obtained from reliability project department.

INCIDENTTITLE: ASSET/PROPERTY at BALCO site at 03 Jan 2024, 9:40 PM
INCIDENTDETAILS: On the 3rd of January 2024, around 2140 hrs., Mr. Radha Raman Yadav, the BCPP I/C, reported an incident that occurred during patrolling at approximately 2130 hrs. Mr. Radharaman Yadav observed footprints in the cooling tower area and discovered an opened concertina coil, with a pipe-like cable hanging over the boundary wall. The information was communicated to the SOC, Plant 1 I/C, and QRT Team, who promptly arrived at around 2200 hrs. A thorough search in both cable rooms resulted in the recovery of approximately 40 meters of copper cables. Unfortunately, the miscreants managed to escape under the cover of darkness. Concurrently, Security Guard Mukesh Yadav, stationed at the Wagon Tripper area, reported suspicious movement at the Silo area conveyor cutting site. The BCPP I/C, Plant 1 I/C, and QRT quickly responded. A comprehensive search led to the discovery of about 50-60 kg of iron scrap from outside the boundary wall. However, the miscreants took advantage of the darkness and dense bushes, managing to escape.

The security team swiftly arrived, conducted a thorough search, and successfully apprehended an intruder identified as Roshan Das (UID-1596705), an employee of M/s Larsen Toubro Limited residing in Kailash Nagar Balco with material approx 25 kg copper cable,1 MS Pipe and 1 LED light. Mr. Roshan Das has been working inside the plant from past 6 months in the project area under Larsen Toubro Limited. This marks his third attempt, and he was caught by the security team. The individual's statement has been recorded, and his ID has been obtained.

INCIDENTTITLE: Material at BALCO site at 07 Oct 2023, 10:30 PM
INCIDENTDETAILS: At approximately 2230 hours on October 7th, 2023, Intelligence team received information from an informant that a worker, identified as Kuldeep Saw, employed at the plant, and recognized by his distinctive orange uniform, was involved in the unauthorized removal and subsequent sale of safety Personal Protective Equipment (PPEs) from the premises. The informant further revealed that Kuldeep Saw had established a pattern of carrying out this illicit activity and was planning to exit the plant between 0100 and 0200 hours on the same night. In response to this information, we immediately initiated a response protocol by deploying a Quick Response Team (QRT) along with the Plant-1 shift in-charge to apprehend the suspect and prevent any further unauthorized removal of safety PPEs. At approximately 0125 hours, the deployed QRT and the Plant-1 in-charge successfully apprehended Mr. Kuldeep Saw, who was in possession of the stolen safety PPEs. Mr. Saw's UID is 1551040, and he is employed by M/s Liz Aluminium Services Private Ltd. During questioning, Mr. Saw admitted to engaging in this activity, confirming that he had been involved in such incidents in 3-4 times in the past, having taken out safety PPEs from the plant and selling them in the external market.

INCIDENTTITLE: Material at BALCO site at 25 Sep 2023, 6:01 PM
INCIDENTDETAILS: On 25.09.2023, at approximately 1801 hours, our intelligence team received critical information regarding the vehicle registered under CG12BJ2780, which was allegedly involved in a plot to steal copper plate, copper angle, and copper rod from the rodding area. This vital intelligence was promptly relayed to Mr. Arbind Mehta, the shift in charge for Plant-1. Around 1830 hours, Mr. Mehta successfully located the vehicle at the alumina gate. Subsequent inspection of the vehicle revealed the presence of copper plate, copper angle, and copper rod concealed beneath the backseat and underneath the vehicle's carpet. Upon conducting a thorough investigation, it was determined that Mr. Brjesh Pratap Singh (Employee ID: 1598119, L&T), who holds the position of supervisor at L&T's rodding site, had observed his colleague, Vishekhar, in the act of removing copper materials from the site. Seizing this illicit opportunity, Mr. Singh decided to pilfer some copper materials from the site and enlisted the assistance of his coworker, Anil Yadav (UID: 1599165, L&T). Together, they transported the stolen copper materials in vehicle (CG12BJ2780), only to be apprehended at the alumina gate, caught red-handed with the purloined goods.

INCIDENTTITLE: Access Related Violations at BALCO site at 2024-06-17 09:00
INCIDENTDETAILS:
On June 17, 2024, while validating Daily Access Data records against CCTV footage, an incident involving multiple In-Punches was flagged. The Security Operations Centre (SOC) discovered that contractor worker Mr. Ajay Nikam (UID 1607216) from M/s Larsen Turbo Limited facilitated the unauthorized entry of his co-worker Mr. Rampravesh Rao (UID 1605562) into the plant premises on June 16, 2022, during the G shift at around 0929 hrs from the project gate.

During the analysis, it was found that Mr. Rampravesh Rao's gate pass was not working. Mr. Ajay Nikam allowed him to enter using his gate pass and subsequently entered using his own pass. Mr. Ajay Nikam was called in for an investigation. During the interrogation, he admitted to allowing Mr. Rampravesh Rao entry because his gate pass was not working, and Mr. Rao was already late for an important task.

INCIDENTTITLE: Intrusion at tamira#1 township TUTICORIN site at 07 Dec 2024, 1:30 AM
INCIDENTDETAILS:
On 07th Dec 2024 at 01:30 hrs. Security guard (Mr. Muniasamy) of Tamira#1 canteen backside duty post observed stones falling sounds from perimeter. When he rushed to the spot, He observed two-person scaled over the perimeter wall and about to jump inside. Then he shouted at them and tossed stones at the miscreants. They shouted back at him not to throw stones and prayed to go away. Then both jumped outside from the wall. Security Guard Mr. Munia Samy gave signal to OS parking guard (Mr. Manikandan V) through long whistles. Then OS parking Guard also rushed to the spot from the outside of perimeter wall. Two miscreants who attempted intrusion fled from the scene. 

Mr. G Mallesham, HoD security, Mr. Subburaj, TPP SO and Mr. Ramamurthy, Copper SO rushed to the spot and further investigation done. Assessed possible entry and exit points. The perimeter found gaps at some places, height was low and no overhead concertina coil.

2. Action taken: 
1.	The Security Team promptly acted upon the incident and foiled the intrusion attempt.
2.	Entire security shift personnel have been alerted and briefed.

3. Recommendations:
3.	Perimeter wall to be strengthened.
4.	Overhead Concertina coil to be placed.
5.	Damaged wall repairing to be done on war foot.
6.	Canal water passage rusted pipes to change to grill or rods and extra gap to be closed.
7.	Scrap lying near the perimeter wall to be removed.

INCIDENTTITLE: Mr. Satish from V Palya Village obstructed the Y-Junction near Gate #2  as on 26 Sep 2025, 7:45 AM.
INCIDENTDETAILS:
On 26th September 2025, at approximately 07:45 hrs, Mr. Satish from V Palya Village obstructed the Y-Junction near Gate #2, which serves as a critical connection between our mine and the BBH Railway Siding. He placed two water tankers at the location, disrupting mining operations. Following discussions, the tankers were removed around 13:00 hrs.
However, at approximately 14:15 hrs, Mr. Satish again blocked the same road using the same two water tankers, claiming possession of an injunction order for the land and stating that Vedanta vehicles were not permitted to use the road. This action resulted in a complete blockade of the route to the BBH Railway Siding, severely impacting iron ore dispatches and staff vehicle movement, thereby causing substantial financial losses to the company.

INCIDENTTITLE: ASSET/PROPERTY at BALCO site at 2025-01-13 13:50
INCIDENTDETAILS: On January 13, 2025, at around 1350hrs, we received critical information by Security Mitra about a vehicle (CG12BH6518) allegedly involved in copper wire theft. This information was relayed to Plant-3 in-charge, Mrs. Pushpanjali Chouhan, and the QRT Team. The security team located the vehicle at the Parsabhata 2W out gate. Upon investigation, Mr. Ajay Kumar Yadav (UID 1594233) from M/s NTPC GE Power Services Private (subcontracted by M/s Feedback Power O&M Services Pvt Ltd, under subcontract by M/s Mandyanti Enterprises) was found involved. A frisking revealed 2.7 kg of copper wire concealed on his body and in his shoes. The suspects were apprehended, and their statements were recorded. INCIDENTTITLE: Unauthorized entry/ Intrusion/Trespassing at VAL J site at 30 Jan 2025, 12:12 PM

INCIDENTTITLE: SOP- LSR Violation at VAL J site at 02 Feb 2025, 4:10 AM
INCIDENTDETAILS: At around 0410hrs, a Loaded Coal Truck (OD23H7565) from Kalyani Transport was unloaded at CPP Hopper Phase-1 without undergoing the mandatory sampling process. Upon interviewing the driver, it was found that he had requested a sampling stamp twice at the Auger-B Sampling Point, but the operator, Padmanath Omath (MMSPL), denied his request and instructed him to proceed for unloading. At the unloading point, Supervisor Rohit Singh (Chennai Radha) also failed to check for the sampling stamp and provided the unloading stamp. The discrepancy was identified by Kartik Shetty at the Challan Office when the driver came for the final out stamp. On preliminary investigation It was revealed that the truck had been unloaded without sampling. The vehicle is currently on hold for further investigation, and all relevant documents have been confiscated by the security team and coal team has been informed about this.

INCIDENTTITLE: ASSET/PROPERTY at TUTICORIN site at 03 Dec 2025, 10:00 AM
INCIDENTDETAILS:
Incident Date & Time: 03.12.2025 at 10:00 hrs
Location: Refinery Area – Cell House 
Description of the Incident
On 2nd Dec at 17:00 hrs a phone call was received from Mr. Prince Prakasam, Lead - Mechanical to Mr. Selvakumar, JSO stating that some bare footprints found near slag yard, Mr. Selvakumar reached the spot, took the photos of footprints and informed to Hod.
On 3rd December 2025 at 10:00 hrs, a phone call was received from Mr. Prince Prakasam again stating that four copper raisers were found missing from the Refinery cell house.
•	Approx. length per raiser: 5 meters
•	Weight per raiser: 120 kg
•	Estimated value per copper raiser: ?1,00,000
A team comprising Mr. Prince Prakasam, Mrs. Judy Fernando, Mr. Sankaranarayanan, Mr. Saravanakumar, and Mr. Selvakumar visited the spot for observation. The team found bare footprints leading towards the PAP–SLF boundary wall and drag marks.
On same day search started in and around the refinery area, at 16:30hrs the team comprising Mr. Saravanakumar, Mr. Vijayaraj & Mr. Albert Jebastin, located four copper raisers in the refinery cell house platforms.
Again, on next day (4th Dec) a phone call was received from Mr. Prince Prakasam stating that three copper raisers were missing, Head Security contacted Mr. Saravanan GM on phone and asked him to confirm how many numbers were missing. He asked for time for couple of days to check the entire site for his team to confirm. 
On 8th Dec Head Security again contacted GM Saravanan at 9:36 am to confirm the incident and he confirmed that three raisers were missing.
On 8th and 9th of Dec’25 searching conducted by security team across the plant in and around the boundary wall and nothing could be located and was informed to COO.
On 9th of Dec ’25 COO, along with Mr. Ramesh Ganesh, Head-Inst., visited the site along with Head security, duty SO Mr. Saravanakumar and user team Mr. Prince Prakasam and Mr. Sankaranarayanan, inspection started at 16:30hrs entire refinery, SLF road, PAP slag yard and up to boundary wall.
Senior team concluded that it could be theft and decided to file a legal complaint.
Additional Observations:
•	No CCTV coverage in the area from Refinery to SLF.
•	No manning in that area since 14.07.2024 due to manpower optimization.
•	Concertina coil was missing (50 mtrs.) near SLF boundary wall (height: 8 feet). 
Findings
1.	Bare footprints from Refinery to SLF boundary wall.
2.	Evidence of drag markings.
3.	Missing concertina coil near SLF boundary wall (height: 8 feet).
Immediate Action Taken
1.	Immediate deployment of 2 guards at Refinery area during dark hours (6 PM to 6 AM).
2.	Concertina coil fixed in the vulnerable area.
3.	Continuous random security patrolling by Duty SO ensured.
4.	Awareness created among guards regarding rounds and whistle blowing every 30 minutes at duty posts to act as deterrence.
Recommendations
1.	Increase lighting in critical areas.
2.	Install CCTV cameras at locations where valuable materials are stored.
3.	Ensure Duty SO has control and monitoring of manpower movement.
4.	Restrict multiple entry access points.
5.	Prepare a checklist of valuable materials and conduct frequent physical verification by user department.
6.	Deploy one security guard round-the-clock in high-value material areas.
7.	Police assistance is being sought through our PR team.
8.	Detailed report will be submitted later as further investigation is in progress.
Spotters:
•	Mr. Prince Prakasam
•	Mr. Sankaranarayanan
Security Team (Incident Response):
•	Mrs. J. Judy Fernando
•	Mr. SaravanaKumar
•	Mr. G Selvakumar

INCIDENTTITLE: Transport stoppage at SMS gate
INCIDENTDETAILS:
On 21-04-2025 at approximately 10:05hrs, local residents from Pilgao and Sarmanas gathered at the Sarmanas gate and blocked the transportation of iron ore. The agitation was triggered due to unresolved local issues, including farmer-related concerns and property disputes specific to the Sarmanas area. The local communities had earlier communicated a resolution deadline of 20th April 2025 to the company. As the issues remained unaddressed by the stipulated date, the villagers resorted to a transport blockade as a form of protest. The situation was brought under control by the local Police Sub-Inspector (PSI). In response, company officials including the CSR Head, Deputy CEO, and Cluster Head arrived at the site and held discussions with the protestors. The Mamlatdar was also contacted and later joined the deliberations.

Following prolonged discussions, an understanding was reached, and transportation activities were resumed at around 1215 hrs.

INCIDENTTITLE: Road #1 truck movement of MEL stopped by Maruthi from V.Palya village at 21 Apr 2025, 8:45 AM
INCIDENTDETAILS:
On 21.04.2025 at around 0845 hrs, Road #1 truck movement of MEL stopped by Maruthi from V.Palya village due to land dispute and Chitradurga BP bus contract termination without any intimation.
Upon received information, alerted security team and informed to admin to divert shift vehicles via king gate and deployed additional security staff and bouncers at the location.
At around 0955 hrs, Informed to Chitradurga Rural Police CI and Hiregruntanur police station by ER/PR.
At around 1000 hrs, JCB brought by Maruthi and same was stopped at BBH Rly siding security gate.
At around 1045 hrs, Maruti also stopped the Road 4 operation and after discussion by security team, cleared from siding area and movement resumed at 1055 hrs, however BSV ground staff not ready to continue the operations and same was communicated to logistics department.
At around 1345 hrs, Police team reached at BBH Rly siding and discussed the matter with Vedanta (Mr. Ravi Nayaka & Mr. Ambarish) and Maruthi.
At around 1545 hrs, MEL Manjunath available at location to briefed about the land details to police.
Post discussion, police advised to lodge police complaint and bring the railway Siding land documents to the police station dated 22.04.2025 for the discussion by all parties.
Also Mr. Arun Shamanur told not to start the siding operation till matter is not resolved.

On 22.04.2025 at around 0935 hrs, again Maruthi came to road #1 BBH siding and stopped the MEL Movement.
At around 1040 hrs, Road #4 truck movement of Vedanta stopped by Maruthi.
Upon received information, alerted security team and deployed additional security staff and bouncers at the location.
At around 1230 hrs, diverted & approx. 50 personnel are available at location (Vedanta Onroll, Workmen, BP Staff including Security & bouncers)
At around 1300 hrs, joint discussion done with Maruthi by Vedanta, MEL team   at BBH Rly Siding office. Meanwhile Chitradurga Rural Police Station CI with his staff and reached at BBH Rly Siding office at 1320 hr.
Joint discussion in presence of police staff done at 1325 hrs.
CI discussed this matter and told to Maruthi for the following points.
1.Do not block the road till issue resolved.
2.Compalint to be given SP Office for the issue by Maruthi and joint survey to be carried out with Govt’ Survey.
Post discussion, Road #4 movement resumed at around 1340 hrs.
At around 1710 hrs, Security, Rly Logistics and ER/PR team visited Chitradurga Rural Police station and met CI.
CI suggested to file one application for the Govt. Survey to be conducted on priority for the land and survey application copy to be handover to CI also.

The security team was present throughout the incident, closely monitoring the situation and prepared to respond to any untoward activity.  All workers left at around 18:00 hrs.

INCIDENTTITLE: Dharna at CLZS(CHANDERIYA) site at 18 Dec 2025, 10:15 AM
INCIDENTDETAILS:
On 18.12.2025, at around 10:15 Hrs,  a local resident, Parmeshwar Jat of Ajoliya Ka Kheda, who alleged that the death of his buffalo was due to Bhunetiya caused by lead pollution from plant operations. Despite initial counselling and engagement, the individual arrived at the main gate with the deceased animal on a tractor-trolley, creating a sensitive law-and-order situation.
Timely intimation to the police ensured their presence at the site. As a precaution, the outer gate was temporarily closed to prevent any forceful entry, while one side of the gate remained operational, ensuring no disruption to routine movement or plant operations. Discussion was held in the presence of CI Gangrar, during which following demands were raised-
1.	Provision of a round-the-clock veterinary doctor at Ajoliya Ka Kheda.
2.	Insurance coverage for domestic animals, sponsored by HZL.
3.	Consideration of the construction of Veterinary Hospital in the vicinity.
They sought the response from HZL within 7 days as the situation was very tense and Parmeshwar Jat produced a bottle containing petrol and threatened self-immolation while standing on the tractor seat. The police acted immediately, seized the petrol bottle, counselled the individual, and successfully defused the situation, preventing any untoward incident.
No written commitment was given, but to de-escalate the situation, it was informed that the matter to be discussed with senior Management and At around 13:15 hrs, the agitators dispersed peacefullyThis is submitted for your kind information and necessary directions to the concerned.

INCIDENTTITLE: IR -  Transporters block the gate 01 tipper movement at IRON ORE KARNATAKA site at 24 Dec 2025, 5:45 AM
INCIDENTDETAILS:
"Incident Summary: Gate#1 Tipper Movement Blockade. 
On 24.12.2025, Gate #1 movement of vedanta and John mines were disrupted by a protest involving new tipper owners and drivers seeking loading permissions. The situation required intervention from logistics, local transport associations, and law enforcement before resuming in the afternoon.

Timeline of Events
 * 06:45 hrs: New tipper owners and drivers halted all Vedanta and John Mines vehicle movements at Gate #1. The logistics department was immediately notified to take corrective action.
 * 07:50 hrs: Protesters erected a temporary shelter (shamiyana) at Muthugudur village. Local authorities at the Chikkajajur police station were alerted.
 * Gate #1 Association members engaged in discussions with the protesters to mediate the blockade and involve the Matha in resolving the dispute.
 * 13:30 hrs: Police personnel arrived on-site to oversee negotiations.
 * 15:30 hrs: Following successful deliberations, the blockade was lifted and normal tipper movement resumed.
Key Meeting Resolutions
To temporarily resolve the conflict, the following points were agreed upon:
 * Immediate Release: All currently loaded and halted tippers are cleared for transit for the day.
 * Loading Restrictions: Effective tomorrow, loading permissions will be restricted to local tippers only; non-local vehicles will be barred.
 * Resolution Window: Association members have been granted a three-week timeline to find a permanent solution regarding loading permissions for the new tipper owners."

INCIDENTTITLE: Unauthorized entry/ Intrusion/Trespassing at CLZS(CHANDERIYA) site at 15 May 2025, 1:20 AM
INCIDENTDETAILS:
Detection and Initial Observation
? At approximately 01:20 hrs., Mr. Manoranjan, the CCTV operator on duty,
observed suspicious movement involving four individuals near the outer side
of the coal yard boundary wall near Tango 13. The individuals appeared to
be inspecting the perimeter and preparing to enter the premises.
? Immediately upon observing the activity, CCTV operator informed the QRTBAAZ,
ASO, and other Security Team. Following this, the security team
swiftly mobilized to respond to the threat.
Response and Ambush
? Following the alert, the security team assembled swiftly and, under the
direction of the Security Officer, planned a strategic ambush.
? Security personnel positioned themselves around the target area to cover all
possible escape routes and awaited further action from the intruders.
Unauthorized Entry and Theft Attempt (01:37 hrs.)
? At approximately 01:37 hrs., two intruders scaled the boundary wall and
entered the premises.
? They proceeded to a waste dump area containing scrap material of value
(lead dross).
? The intruders began filling bag with the lead dross and threw the bag over
the wall to their two accomplices waiting outside.
? This theft attempt was closely monitored by the ambush team.
Apprehension of Intruders (02:05 hrs)
? While the theft was ongoing, the ambush team and QRT moved in.
? Upon seeing the security personnel, the intruders attempted to flee.
? The security team gave immediate chase and apprehended both intruders
within the premises.
? Meanwhile, the accomplices outside began pelting stones at the security
personnel in an effort to aid the escape.
? The security team responded accordingly to deter the attackers, after which
the accomplices outside fled the scene under cover of darkness.
? No major injuries were reported, and the situation was brought under
control.

The incident has been escalated to the concerned HR department for further disciplinary action and necessary proceedings.

The roadblock was cleared at 16:00 hrs. after a mutual agreement was reached in the presence of police at Chas mufassil police station .

 Speed Control: They want shift vehicles to maintain a controlled speed on village roads.
 Road Maintenance: They are demanding the cleaning of vegetation/bushes from both sides of the roads.
 Dust Compensation: The locals are seeking compensation for dust pollution caused by the vehicles."

INCIDENTTITLE: Material at BALCO site at 21 Mar 2026, 4:20 PM
INCIDENTDETAILS: On 21st March 2026 at 16:20 hrs, intelligence input was received regarding suspicious activity at Potline-1, Section-2. The Intelligence Team was immediately alerted and reached the location immediately. The team closely monitored the suspect’s activity and observed an individual attempting to cut a copper cable. The Intelligence Team took immediate action and caught the individual red-handed along with the stolen material. Information about the theft incident was immediately shared with all concerned authorities. Upon receiving the information, Plant-02 S/IC, along with the Quick Reaction Team (QRT), reached the site and carried out a detailed investigation. During the investigation, it was found that Mr. Sanker Srivas (UID No. 10700), an employee of M/s Raju Engineering, was involved in the theft attempt. The accused was attempting to steal approximately 45 kg of copper cable, valued at ?33,120/-, belonging to RMPL contractor material. During the search, one steel knife was recovered from the possession of the accused. As part of consequential management, the statement of the accused was recorded. The accused was thereafter handed over to BALCO Police Station for further legal action. An FIR was jointly lodged by RMPL and the Security Team for investigation and necessary action.

During the checking process, 05 Poclain teeth, valued at Rs. 7000/- were found concealed inside the vehicle, being taken out of the premises without an NRGP and without the knowledge or approval of the concerned department. 5. Non deployment of security personnel for a long time increased risk of theft."

INCIDENTTITLE: ASSET/PROPERTY at IRON AND POWER site at 06 Jan 2026, 1:10 AM
INCIDENTDETAILS:
At approximately 0110 hours, KEC security guard Vidhya Dhar Bauri (ID: 539553, Mobile No.: 7209592109) reported to the SCCC that five unidentified suspects had entered the Tippler Project area. Upon receipt of the information, the SCCC immediately informed the Security Shift IC, who promptly alerted QRT-01. The QRT team reached the location without delay. However, upon noticing the arrival of the QRT vehicle, all five suspects fled from the area.
The Security Shift IC, along with QRT-02 and the Traffic Team, also reached the location and conducted a thorough search of the area; however, the suspects had already escaped. During further investigation, it was observed that a large quantity of copper cable was present at the site. The suspects had cut the copper cable into five smaller bundles and had attempted to remove them by tying the bundles with their mufflers. While fleeing the scene, the suspects encountered KEC security guard Md. Sabir Ansari (ID: 529678). When the guard raised an alarm, the suspects attempted to assault him. Meanwhile, QRT-01 arrived at the location, prompting the suspects to abandon the copper bundles along the way and flee the area. Despite repeated and intensive search operations carried out by the Security Shift IC, QRT-01, QRT-02, and the Traffic Team, the suspects could not be traced. The five recovered copper bundles, measuring approximately 35–40 meters of copper cable and valued at approximately Rs. 35,000, were secured and transported to the Security Control Room for safekeeping and further necessary action. The incident has been duly intimated to Mr. Sachin Kumar, HR In-Charge, KEC (Mobile No.: 9771784300).

INCIDENTTITLE: Material at VAL J site at 15 Mar 2026, 4:30 PM
INCIDENTDETAILS:

5.Poor control over scrap/material handling and disposal process."

INCIDENTTITLE: ASSET/PROPERTY at MEL site at 11 May 2026, 7:05 AM
INCIDENTDETAILS:
On 11th May 2026 at around 0615hrs, a theft incident was unfoiled at the Main Gate during routine frisking procedures. Mr. Ramesh, Fire Supervisor was found concealing a fan motor housing along with the motor assembly and tried to unlawfully take the material away from the premises.

The security officer immediately detained the individual and informed the Lead Security. The material was recovered in full, and no loss to the company property occurred. Preliminary inquiry indicates deliberate intent by Mr. Ramesh to commit theft by concealing the item. 

The individual statement was taken, and Gate Pass was collected from him and sent outside the Plant Premises. Further Lead Security went to the incident scene for checking the area. It was found that a Fan was replaced in recent past (March Month) view repair and only the fan blades were found at the Fire store. It was ascertained from the other workforce working at fire office that the Motor along with the Housing is missing today.  

The issue was highlighted to higher authorities for further investigation and necessary disciplinary/legal action.
